liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dancin' in the Streets** (4 reviews): Dancin' has terrific jamming and an interesting transition into Franklin's Tower, credited to Phil; At the end of Dancin', Weir takes over with an intro into Franklin's until Garcia reasserts the tonic [13][19][20][21]
- **Johnny B. Goode** (2 other sources): First track of the Johnny B. Goode is the encore from 11/8/79, not this show; The Johnny B. Goode from the previous night was removed from the start of CD 1 [1][5]
- **Lazy Lightnin'** (2 reviews): Garcia plays a blazing jam in the Lazy Lightnin' into Supplication pairing; Reviewer calls this Lazy Lightnin' into Supplication among the best ever, having heard nearly all versions [10][16]
- **Althea** (2 reviews): Althea is loose and was newly played at this point; the first set ends with a huge Jack Straw; The Althea converted a listener who preferred early-70s shows [13][17]
- **He's Gone** (2 reviews): The jam out of He's Gone is the intense Gloria jam the band played a few times; A hot Gloria-type jam closes out He's Gone [13][16]
- **Easy to Love You** (1 review): Reviewer hears this Easy to Love You as unusual, possibly with different lyrics from normal [10]
- **Franklin's Tower** (1 review): Around 10:47 into Franklin's, Garcia trills heavily and Weir then steps up [19]
- **Estimated Prophet** (1 review): Brent is first out of Estimated Prophet, and his instrument sounds wonderful [19]

## The recordings

- **gd79-11-09.sbd.stern.318.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 23 songs; 175 min; rated 4.52/5 by 33 [1]. Said about its sound: Soundboard sound is described as extremely clear and crisp, comparable to the 12/28/79 show; Some funkiness in the first set sound and the right channel, which is tolerable; 1979 sound is cleaner and more modern, with Brent's keyboards noted [1][10][16][17][18][21]
- **gd1979-11-09.150448.sbd.gems.flac16**: soundboard; 22 songs; 181 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [2]. Said about its sound: Persistent low-level tape grime in the right channel that does not detract from the music; First Althea note is cut in; a small SBD patch in Jack Straw, and small audience patches in He's Gone and Bertha [2]
- **gd1979-11-09.aud-unknown.andrewf.79702.flac16**: audience recording; 23 songs; 183 min; rated 4.2/5 by 5 [3]. Said about its sound: Audience recording has two small cuts: near the end of Estimated and near the end of Drums [3]
- **gd1979-11-09.sbd.stern.tetzeli.fix-318.34936.reflac.flac16**: soundboard; 22 songs; 170 min; rated 4.4/5 by 10 [5]. Said about its sound: Overlap between CDs 2 and 3 removed so Dancin' into I Need a Miracle plays seamlessly [5]

## Around the show

- Set one has over twelve minutes of long tunings [2]
- Reviewer says comparable peak moments occur in shows shortly before and after this one [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd79-11-09.sbd.stern.318.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Soundboard via A. Stern, taken through MR, DAT, Sonic Solutions to CD; previously circulated to abgd [1]
- **gd1979-11-09.150448.sbd.gems.flac16**: transferred by Speed Corrections by Jason Chastain Audio Mastering by Jamie Waddell; source: Soundboard [2]
- **gd1979-11-09.aud-unknown.andrewf.79702.flac16**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Andrew F; source: AUD (unknown equipment and lineage, see note below) [3]. Also: Made from tapes lent by Joey Browning; Soundforge used for fades, level adjustments and small edits [3]
- **gd1979-11-09.sbd.stern.tetzeli.fix-318.34936.reflac.flac16**: transferred by Bill Tetzeli; source: SBD> Cm> Cass> Dat> Sound Forge> CD > WAV > SHN > WAV > FLAC [5]

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead War Memorial Auditorium - November 9, 1979](https://www.dead.net/show/november-9-1979) [23]
- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead War Memorial Auditorium - November 9, 1979](https://www.dead.net/show/november-9-1979) [24]
